translation: It is this perpetuation of the data of history, handed on to us first by the generation that precedes us, that we call civilization.

translation: The way in which the people in any group do things, make and use tools, get along with one another and with other groups, the words they use and the way they use them to express thoughts, and the thoughts they think — all of these we call the group's culture.
basis: K&K's own English rendering, printed by K&K after the French in footnote 18a (text layer, PDF p. 54); printed page not verified

translation: Culture is the result of the mental activity of man, objectified, matter-bound spirit.
basis: assistant translation of the German as printed (text layer, PDF p. 67); printed page not verified; user to verify

translation: In its deepest essence culture consists in the inner formation of the human mind, and in the outer formation of the body and of nature insofar as the latter is guided by the mind. Thus culture, like everything mental, is something immanent, something thoroughly inner, and as such not directly accessible to external observation.
